(Search snippet content — Bank of England / rate-decision preview, mid-late July 2026)

The Monetary Policy Committee announces its next decision on Thursday 30 July 2026 at 12:00 noon, alongside a full Monetary Policy Report and a Governor's press conference at 1:00pm.
Bank Rate is currently 3.75%, held on 18 June 2026 in a 7-2 vote, with Megan Greene and Huw Pill voting for a hike to 4.00%.
Market-implied probability of no change at 30 July is around 86% (SONIA futures, mid-July); a rise to 4.00% implied at ~14%.
UK CPI held at 2.8% in May; services inflation rose to 3.7%, keeping the MPC cautious.
The recent rebound in oil prices due to renewed Middle East hostilities prompted traders to bring forward rate-rise expectations; markets priced in two rate hikes by March 2027 as of 22 July.
On 9 July the Bank's Chief Economist (Huw Pill) said publicly that interest rates will need to rise over the coming year.
